To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a SILAC-based mass spectrometry (MS) approach to probe mammalian ribosomes and used it to obtain a comparative characterization of ribosomes from multiple mammalian cells, which identified a set of components with a strong enrichment in RNA-binding proteins, and that we further validated the association with polyribosome for several ribosomal proteins and demonstrated that enrichment at the mammalian ribosome can depend on cell line, genetics, or cell stimulation.

the mammalian ribosome contains a diverse array of RNA-binding proteins that are frequently amplified in cancer, and that the composition of the mammalian polyribosomes is dynamic and can depend on cellular stimulus.
we developed an experimental approach that allowed us to characterize the mammalian ribosome proteome in a variety of cellular contexts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mammalian proteome that associates with the ribosome.

the identification and characterization of the riboproteins in the cell, the factors that influence their association with the ribosome, and their potential roles as regulators of biological processes.
the characterization and analysis of the mammalian proteome, with a particular focus on ribosomal components and the role of the riboproteomes in disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the riboproteomics approach described herein provides a platform for probing mammalian ribosomes in an unbiased and quantitative manner, and the results presented herein provide a foundation for the further exploration of the role of the mammalian translational machinery in health and disease.
the riboproteomic analysis of the mammalian cell line has revealed a number of interesting and potentially important findings.
riboproteome analysis is a powerful approach for the characterization of riboproteomes and their regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a set of proteins that are associated with riboproteomes and that are enriched for genetic alterations in cancer, with distinct patterns of genetic alteration.
the ribosome is a dynamic, highly regulated organelle with a diverse array of associated proteins, many of which are genetically altered in cancer.
we have identified the riboproteins in mammalian cells and that these are enriched for RNA-binding proteins, and that there is a strong correlation between riboproteome and polyribosome association.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the riboproteomes are not static and are highly regulated.
the riboproteomes of cells are not static, but rather dynamic entities whose components can change in response to a variety of stimuli.

ribosomes are not simply passive participants in translation but rather actively participate in a variety of cellular processes, including transcription and translation, RNA metabolism and processing, protein folding, and signaling.
